response.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS member_count FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city), shares AS (SELECT city, member_count, member_count * 1.0 / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share FROM city_counts), stats AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), above AS (SELECT s.member_count, s.share FROM shares s, stats st WHERE s.share > st.avg_share) SELECT AVG(a.member_count) AS avg_count, AVG(a.share) AS avg_share, AVG(a.share - st.avg_share) AS avg_share_above_average FROM above a, stats st;

assumptions.assumption: A city is identified by zip_code.city alone, so same-named cities in different states are merged into one city.
Attendance rows whose member has no zip that matches zip_code are excluded by the inner joins.
The average share is taken over the per-city rows, and the 'amount above average' is the mean of (share - average share) over the cities whose share exceeds that average.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat a city as the pair (city, state), so same-named cities in different states are counted separately.
alternatives.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city, z.short_state, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS member_count FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city, z.short_state), shares AS (SELECT city, short_state, member_count, member_count * 1.0 / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share FROM city_counts), stats AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), above AS (SELECT s.member_count, s.share FROM shares s, stats st WHERE s.share > st.avg_share) SELECT AVG(a.member_count) AS avg_count, AVG(a.share) AS avg_share, AVG(a.share - st.avg_share) AS avg_share_above_average FROM above a, stats st;
